post.description:
Ask a job to stop, and answer immediately.

`cancelled: true` means the request was *made*, not that the job has
stopped: a job finishes between frames, and after its grace period the
watchdog closes the record anyway. A client learns the ending from the
socket or from `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}` — not by blocking here.

Cancelling a job that has already finished is a refusal, because a UI that
offers a cancel button for a finished job has a bug, and an endpoint that
shrugged would hide it.

post.description:
Execute one command and journal it, or say precisely why not.

A refused edit costs the user nothing — not even their redo future: the
command is only recorded once it has succeeded. A journalling failure rolls
the edit back and says so, because an edit we cannot replay is an edit we
must not pretend to have kept.

post.description:
Queue an export, and answer with the job that will do it.

The project is read **now** and frozen into the job: an edit made while the
export runs changes the editor, not the file being written. That is a
promise a user can plan around, and it is why the body carries a value
rather than a project id.

Returns:
    202 with the submission; 404 when no project with that id is open; 422
    when the request names a container, a codec or a range the domain
    cannot build; 503 when every export slot is busy — in which case
    nothing was queued and trying again is the remedy.

post.description:
Plan what the project needs, submit it, and answer with the jobs.

Called as often as it likes — on an import, on a panel repaint, on a timer —
because **what is missing is a pure question**: an artefact already held is
simply not planned, so a second call when nothing has changed queues nothing
and is nearly free.

Returns:
    202 with the jobs that were queued — possibly an empty list, which is
    the ordinary answer for a project that is already up to date; 404 when
    no project with that id is open; 503 when the executor has no room, in
    which case the jobs that did fit are named and the rest are not queued.

get.description:
Composite one frame and send it as an image.

The frame is composited by the same code the export uses, at the project's
own size, and scaled down to what the panel can show — never up: pixels
above 1:1 are not information, and zoom is a display concern, not a request
for more of them.

A layer whose media is offline is **not** a failure: the frame is drawn
without it and the asset ids are listed in `X-Nova-Preview-Gaps`, because a
panel that showed an error instead of a frame would hide the nineteen clips
that are fine.

post.description:
Have the next few frames decoded before they are asked for.

Warming is its own request rather than a side effect of :func:`preview_frame`
because it is work the user has not asked to see: done inside the frame
request it would add fifteen decodes of latency to the one frame being
waited for, and done on every request it would warm the frames the user is
scrubbing *away* from.

The response carries the pool's `seeks`, which is the number that says
whether scrubbing is healthy: one per clip per run, not one per frame.

delete.description:
Forget derived bytes, and say how much disk came back.

Losing the cache costs a rebuild and nothing else (ADR-0015 rule 6: it is
disposable), which is why this is a button and not a confirmation about
projects. Proxies and thumbnails come back the next time something asks for
them.

The bytes go before the row, per entry, so an interrupted deletion leaves an
entry pointing at nothing — which the cache already reads as a miss — rather
than unreachable bytes no entry names and no eviction will ever reclaim.

get.description:
Every derived artefact this install has made, oldest use first.

Here rather than under a project, because the cache **is** install-wide:
two projects that share a source share its proxy, and a user asking "how
much disk is this costing me" is asking about the machine, not about a
file.

The order is the order eviction will take them in, which is what an
inspector and a byte budget both want to read off the same list.
